### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**10** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f2d1cc99836aa52fd190e48f140d7b9fda9f2944` — the merge of head `baf8e225450a844e7c7e0401c5efea54b2f9d7ad` into base `8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin f2d1cc99836aa52fd190e48f140d7b9fda9f2944 && git checkout f2d1cc99836aa52fd190e48f140d7b9fda9f2944

git fetch origin 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214 baf8e225450a844e7c7e0401c5efea54b2f9d7ad && git checkout -B drift-repro 8dfd1265f006ea0a6f727fa966e980ede57b4214 && git merge --no-ff baf8e225450a844e7c7e0401c5efea54b2f9d7ad
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `baf8e225450a844e7c7e0401c5efea54b2f9d7ad`
Local-runs: none

Read-only, at 2026-10-22T19:42Z: card #25267 (body and both comments, the claim 6348364574 and the os-dev-report 6349466484), PR #25275 (body, file list, net diff against `main`, its one comment), the check-runs on the head, and these files at the head: `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts` (whole: `buildEnv` / `CEL_ENV_OPTIONS`, `buildScopedEnv`, `buildTypedEnv`, `runProgram`, `firstUndeclaredReference`, `collectCelRootIdentifiers`, `parseCelToAst` / `parseCelToAstWithReason`, `inferCelType`, `firstTypeMismatch`, `rewriteNullableTernary`, `rewriteIndexedHas` / `indexedHasSelection` / `HAS_CALL_RE`, `celEngine.compile` / `evaluate`), `packages/formula/src/cel-has-indexed-receiver.test.ts`, `.changeset/25267-cel-has-indexed-receiver.md`, `packages/formula/src/validate.ts` (`validateExpression`, `inferExpressionType`), `packages/formula/src/unknown-function.ts`, `packages/formula/src/index.ts` and `package.json` (exports), `packages/lint/src/validate-visibility-predicates.ts` (`hasCallSpans` / `maskHasCalls` / `firstUnboundReference`, the #13594 function-existence call), `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (the predicate-slot `validateExpression` calls), `packages/lint/src/flow-variable-scope.ts` and `flow-cel-root-scope.ts` (the `firstUndeclaredReference` callers), `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (`registerFlow`'s predicate pass), `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts` (eligibility evaluate), `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts` (`guardOf`) and its test at line 201, `packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts` (the dialect table). Rules read: AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3, Prime Directives 10 / 12 / 14), `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (ruling A on #25105), `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` header, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` (`REVIEW_FACES`, `servedTierStands`, the template), `docs/releases-maintenance.md` (release-note sections). cel-js 8.0.0's own source is not installed in this container, so its macro and optional-type semantics are taken from the parity pins in the new test and the check-runs, not from a reading of the library.

**Served-tier note.** The brief asked for `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this line. `reviewFace` on the PR's three paths returns the `declaration` face (no schema path, no governed path, no `(narrowing)` arm), and `record-recognisers.mjs` is exact by face in both directions (`servedTierStands`; `--template --face declaration` prints `TIER_DEFAULT`), so the token the face maps to is the one written here. The session that rendered it runs at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; that is a fact about the reviewer, not the line. The declaration face carries no `Scope:` key line by the template's own rule, so the files read are listed in prose above.

### ① Derived judgments

Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-22T19:42Z: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, every `Lint ·` and `Type Check ·` lane except `Type Check · workspace`, and the four card/claim checks are `success`; `Test Core (1/6 … 6/6)` and `Type Check · workspace` are still `in_progress` — reported as pending, not waited for. The full-battery lanes are `skipped` on a PR run, as designed. No check-run is red.

1. **`rewriteIndexedHas` — presence semantics at every entry point: right.** `indexedHasSelection` fires only on a `call` node named `has` with exactly one argument whose node is a `.` select and whose `.`/`.?` chain bottoms out in a node that is not an `id` (an `[]` index, a call, a list/map literal). The lowering replaces the call with `rcall hasValue` on a `.?` select over the same `(receiver, field)` pair — the receiver is kept as an ordinary select chain, so an absent key before the last step still evaluates `receiver.key` and faults `No such key` (fault, not `false`), and only the final `.?f` answers `false`. That is the CEL spec's definition of `has(e.f)` over optional selection. It is applied at the five sites where cel-js's checker or evaluator sees the source: `compile`, `evaluate`, `firstUndeclaredReference`, `inferCelType`, `firstTypeMismatch`. Every environment those sites use carries `enableOptionalTypes: true` (`CEL_ENV_OPTIONS`, `buildScopedEnv`, both arms of `buildTypedEnv`), so the lowered `.?` / `hasValue()` form parses and checks in each. The parse-only front end (`parseCelToAstWithReason` / `parseCelToAst`, `collectCelRootIdentifiers`, the pushdown lowering) is deliberately untouched, so the lint's AST consumers (`hasCallSpans`, null-guard reading, root collection) still see the authored `has(…)` call — verified against `validate-visibility-predicates.ts`, which masks `has(…)` spans from `parseCelToAst`'s AST and only then calls `firstUndeclaredReference` on a source that no longer contains `has(`, so the rewrite is a no-op there by the regex gate.
2. **Bare name and index-as-last-step still refused: right.** `has(status)`: the argument is an `id`, not a `.` select, so no rewrite; `has(record.items[0])`: the argument is an `[]` node, not `.`, so no rewrite; both reach cel-js's own macro and still fault `has() invalid argument` at `compile`, `validateExpression` and `evaluate` — pinned by the controls test. `has(record.a.b)` (identifier root) is left to cel-js unchanged.
3. **No already-evaluating expression changes its answer: right.** The rewrite touches only a `has()` call whose selection chain is not identifier-rooted, and every such call faulted at parse-time macro expansion before this change — the card measured `evaluate` answering `ok: false`, and `runProgram` runs no separate `check()`, so the fault was the macro's own. The cheap gate `HAS_CALL_RE` excludes `.has(` (a member call, `rcall` in the AST) and longer names; a `has(` inside a string literal passes the gate, parses to no `call` node and is left unchanged. The memo is keyed on source alone and the rewrite reads no scope, so caching is sound. Order of composition is consistent: `rewriteIndexedHas` is innermost at every site, and the later passes (`rewriteNullableTernary`, `rewriteTemporalEquality`, `rewriteFaultedOperands`) parse through optional-type-enabled environments and match no `.?` node, so they neither break on nor rewrite the lowered form.
4. **`firstUndeclaredReference` reports more, never less, and only on sources `compile` already refused: right.** `has(a[0].b) && status == 'x'` used to answer `null` (the macro fault took cel-js's single error slot) and now answers `status`. Its consumers (`flow-variable-scope`, `flow-cel-root-scope`, `validateExpression`'s bare-ref arm) can therefore gain a finding on such a source, but every such source was already refused by the `validateExpression` → `compile` pass at the same lint/registration step, so no metadata that published before is refused now. `inferCelType` now returns `bool` for the form instead of `null`; `firstTypeMismatch` keeps its verdict (`UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE` matched neither the old macro fault nor any new message).
5. **Accept-set change, measured from the diff.** Widened: every slot judged through `celEngine.compile` — `validateExpression('predicate', …)` on object validation/visibility rules, flow conditions, action and sharing-rule predicates and hook predicates, AND `validateExpression('value', …)` on flow assignment values, `Field.formula` and seed dynamic values (the `value` role takes the same `compile` branch at `validate.ts:988`), plus `inferExpressionType`. Narrowed: nothing. The page/view `visibleWhen` gate is unchanged in both directions — its syntax verdict is `parseCelToAst`'s (parsed before, parses now) and its one adopted `check()` verdict, `firstUnknownFunctionCall`, filters `compile`'s message on the no-overload vocabulary, which neither `has() invalid argument` nor a clean compile matches. The engine and the publish validator now agree on this class, which is the card's acceptance line.
6. **Public surface: unchanged.** `rewriteIndexedHas` is exported from `cel-engine.ts` for its test, but `@objectstack/formula` publishes only `.` → `dist/index.*`, and `index.ts` does not re-export it — the same standing as `rewriteNullableTernary`. No spec artifact moves; `Check Changeset` and the spec gates are green.
7. **Changeset prose — one incompleteness, not a wrong declaration.** The "What widens" bullet names the five predicate slots and omits the `value`-role slots named in item 5. The claim is narrower than the behaviour (the safe direction under Prime Directive 10's corollary), so it is a note for the dev, not a FAIL item: one clause on the bullet would make the changelog sentence complete.
8. **Test file.** Nine pins, imported from source (no `dist` leg); the parity test compares the lowered form against cel-js's own identifier-rooted `has()` over ten value kinds × two depths by outcome kind and first message line, which is the right oracle given that the library's semantics cannot be read here. The ablation reported in the PR body (8 failed / 1 passed with the rewrite short-circuited, controls staying green) is consistent with the pins' shape.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — **true.** The line answers 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (`clause2-line.mjs`). Measured from the diff, the publish accept set is relaxed: strings every `compile`-backed door refused before are accepted now (item 5). The public face is unchanged (item 6); the accept-set half alone makes the answer yes, and `(widening)` is the only arm that fits.
- `Metadata-protocol: added` — **true.** AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 defines the kind as "the change to what a metadata author can write — a new key, accepted value or metadata type is `added`". An author can now write `has(a[0].b)` in a predicate or value slot where the platform refused it: a newly accepted value. No key is removed, no requirement tightened, no meaning or default changed, so neither `narrowed` nor `semantic` applies.
- `@objectstack/formula: minor` — **true.** Same step: "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves"; ruling A on #25105 (`clause2-line.mjs` header): "`minor` when the protocol an author writes against is added to". The diff moves only `@objectstack/formula`.
- **The dev's open question (A vs B): A, decided by the rules, no escalation.** Reading B — "an implementation gap in an already-declared CEL dialect, so `no` / `none` / `patch`" — would need a rule that keys the level on the declared dialect rather than on what the platform accepts. The repo's rules key it on measurement: the Clause-② line is "measured from the diff" (the claim comment says so; `record-recognisers.mjs` reads every face "off the pull request's committed tree, never off a seat's statement"), the Metadata-protocol kind is defined over what an author "can write", and Prime Directive 10's corollary makes the enforced set the platform's claim ("keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement"). The repo's own contract text also declared the narrower behaviour as the platform's — the `guardOf` docblock in `packages/spec` says an index anywhere in a `has()` argument "is refused when it runs" — so "already-declared CEL dialect" is not what the spec package said. Reader-facing consequence: `added` places the entry under 「新增能力」 in the release body (`docs/releases-maintenance.md`), where an upgrading author learns the form is accepted; B would file it under 「其他修复」 and hide exactly that. The `fix(formula):` summary prefix beside `minor` is fine: the level follows the kind alone.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag: `Clause-②` / `Metadata-protocol` reading (open question).** Answered above: A stands; keep `yes (widening)`, `added`, `minor`.
- **Flag: route taken (evaluate, not refuse).** Right choice under Prime Directive 12 — the metadata is spec-compliant CEL, so the consumer was the thing to fix, not the author; and it takes the engine fix without a lint change, since every type verdict already flows through `@objectstack/formula`. The card's "engine and publish validator agree" acceptance is met for this class.
- **Flag: error excerpts quote the lowered source** on a runtime fault inside a lowered call. Accepted: it is the same property `rewriteNullableTernary` already has, the authored `has(…)` stays in every parse-only surface and in `issue.source` at lint, and the class of fault (`No such key` on an intermediate step) names the key the author wrote.
- **Flag: removal note** (drop `rewriteIndexedHas` and its five call sites when cel-js lifts the identifier-root restriction). Fine as a code-comment note; nothing to do now.
- **Flag: the sibling class stays open (out-of-scope finding 1).** `has(status)` and `has(record.items[0])` on a page or view `visibleWhen` still publish with 0 findings and fault at runtime, so the console still fails open on them. **Answer: maintainer.** Closing it means adopting a second `check()` complaint on the page/view rule, which ruling #13594 refinement 3 reserves: 「只拒未知函数裁定,⛔ 不搬运 `check()` 的其他抱怨。」 (quoted verbatim from `validate-visibility-predicates.ts`). No seat may reverse that; it needs the maintainer's word on which of the two remedies the card's "Wanted" section allows (adopt the `has() invalid argument` verdict on that rule, or refuse at publish with the `in`-form message). The dedupe pass over the 106 open cards at 2026-10-22T19:42Z found no card for this class (only #25267 itself and #20178, a different `visibleWhen` scope finding), so the ruling request needs a carrier: a class-(c) card with the dev's measured repro (`validateVisibilityPredicates` 0 findings against the `record.x === 1` control; `celEngine.evaluate` faulting on both), addressed to the maintainer for the ruling before any seat implements. Not this PR.
- **Flag: stale `guardOf` docblock and test title (out-of-scope finding 2).** `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-value-slot-template.ts` (`guardOf`, "an index anywhere in its argument … is refused when it runs") and `flow-value-slot-template.test.ts:201` ("`has()` refuses one at run time") state a reason that is false after this PR; the behaviour they explain stays right, because a path ending in an index (`vars.rows[0]`, one of the chain's own steps) is still refused and an out-of-range index faults rather than answering `false`. **Answer: card, and it cannot ride this PR.** Two reasons: the claim's file surface is `packages/formula/src/`, `packages/lint/src/`, their tests and one changeset, "stop on breach", and `packages/spec/src/**` is a breach; and `reviewFace` reads `packages/spec/src/**` (tests excepted) as the schema face, so adding that file would move this PR onto `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`'s schema face and invalidate this record. It is a docs-only, S-class `domain:spec` follow-up (two comment edits, no behaviour), and it needs a card rather than an acceptance note because the note dies with this PR while a false claim in the contract package is text the next agent reasons from.
